jobs.title: Research Operations Lead, Biology
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the team Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries. The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery. About the role We are hiring a Research Operations Lead to be the operational backbone of our team: the person who makes sure scientists can walk in every morning and get straight to science. You'll take on the operational systems we've started — procurement, inventory, safety, equipment, space — make them better, and scale them as the lab and its needs grow. We're hiring for trajectory as much as for what you've already done: the scope of this role will grow with the size of the team, and we want someone who's excited by that. This role is a rare opportunity to build the operational foundation of Anthropic's biology team and to grow with it. The systems you put in place will shape how a frontier AI company does experimental biology for years to come. If you're energized by high-ownership operational work in the service of ambitious science, we'd love to hear from you. Key responsibilities Own day-to-day operations end to end: ordering and inventory, equipment scheduling and upkeep, consumables, shipping and receiving, and general space organization Build on and extend the operational systems a growing group needs: procurement workflows, inventory and sample tracking, equipment maintenance and calibration schedules, onboarding and training, SOPs Manage facilities and space: coordinate buildouts, moves, and equipment installs; act as the primary interface to building management, contractors, and Anthropic's central Workplace and IT teams Own the operating budget: track spend against plan, run the capital equipment purchasing process, and partner with Finance on forecasting and reporting Manage vendor and supplier relationships: including contract research organizations: source and qualify vendors, negotiate quotes and service contracts, schedule preventive maintenance and field-service visits, and hold suppliers to their commitments Minimum qualifications Have managed the day-to-day operations of a life sciences lab — equipment, inventory, ordering, safety, space, and scheduling Have hands-on procurement and vendor management experience: sourcing suppliers, negotiating quotes and service contracts, and coordinating field-service and maintenance technicians Have tracked and managed an operating budget: purchase orders, invoices, spend-vs-plan, and capital requests Preferred qualifications Are the person everyone in your group already comes to when something is broken, missing, late, or unclear — and you like being that person Enjoy engaging with scientists on the science itself — you want to understand what's happening at the bench well enough to anticipate needs Are results-oriented and practical and pick up slack even when it goes outside your job description Enjoy a role that stretches from the hands-on to the strategic, and are comfortable when priorities shift quickly and feedback is direct Lab operations or lab management experience in a biotech, pharma, diagnostics, or life-sciences startup environment, including exposure to how those organizations build new functions and processes end to end A degree in the life sciences and prior research experience at the bench People-management experience: hiring, onboarding, and supervising operations or facilities staff Experience supporting a team through significant growth in headcount, footprint, or capability, including utilities, permitting, and equipment Familiarity with liquid-handling platforms, including their service, calibration, and consumable needs Experience selecting and administering inventory management, sample tracking, equipment scheduling, or ELN systems Capital equipment lifecycle management experience — evaluation, purchase, qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ), service contracts, and decommissioning Experience with regulated shipping and receiving of biological materials, including import/export, permits, and material transfer agreements Experience using AI tools for efficient team and process management (e.g., Claude Cowork) The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $210,000 — $260,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

The execution planner will interact with internal and external supply sites, logistics, and other supply chain teams. Responsibilities include assisting in the development of supply strategies, helping to create and execute supply plans, and identifying and reporting any risks or constraints that may affect product availability. Supply Planning and Execution: Develop and manage supply plans for materials related to product portfolios Support coordination with internal and external manufacturing sites to help balance customer service with operational efficiency. Maintain accurate inventory levels, ensuring purchase orders are up to date for Drug Substance, Drug Product and Finished goods to meet demand Customer and Stakeholder Engagement: Build and maintain relationships with global and local supply chain teams and market stakeholders, collaborating to ensure continuity of supply and identify potential risks Attend supply chain meetings to ensure runs effectively Monitor changes in demand, communicate with stakeholders to adjust production plans, and incorporate these changes into site production schedules Risk Management & Problem Solving: risks related to regulatory or artwork changes Metrics and Reporting: Track and report on key supply chain performance metrics such as backorders, inventory compliance, and PO accuracy Provide input into inventory projections, budget processes, and root cause analysis for any supply issues Contribute to monthly and quarterly stock overviews, identifying any inventory risks or supply disruptions Projects & Continuous Improvement: Participate in supply chain improvement projects and other initiatives to optimize supply chain processes Support new product introductions, government tender supply programs, and clinical supply requests when required Ensure that master data is accurately maintained and continuously updated in collaboration with relevant teams Digital Acumen, Analytics, and Learning Leverages visualization and data contextualization tools including Excel and BI platforms (e.g., Tableau, Power BI), integrated APS capabilities, and BMS platforms to monitor KPIs, perform root cause analysis, review best action analysis and provide data-driven decision support. jobs.description: Career Category Manufacturing Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Be part of Amgen's newest and most advanced drug substance manufacturing plant. When completed, the Amgen FleX batch facility will combine the latest in disposable technologies with traditional stainless steel equipment to allow for maximum flexibility in operations The FleX Batch facility will not only feature the best in-class drug substance manufacturing technologies with embedded industry 4.0 capabilities, but it will also integrate sustainability innovations to reduce carbon and waste, as part of Amgen's plan to be a carbon-neutral company by 2027. Process Analytical Engineer What you will do In this vital role, you will join the Facilities & Engineering (F&E) group and be responsible for planning, executing, and documenting the qualification, calibration, and routine maintenance of laboratory systems for cGMP Quality Control laboratory facilities at Amgen North Carolina (ANC). This role includes hands-on troubleshooting and root cause analysis for analytical and laboratory systems, coordination of vendor support and repairs, execution and tracking of calibration, maintenance, and requalification activities through the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) Maximo, and direct support for manufacturing operations to improve equipment uptime and reliability. You will also author, own, and approve Validation Life Cycle documents for computer-related systems, including responsibility for Data Integrity testing and business administration of laboratory computer-related systems. Support commissioning, qualification, validation, and system lifecycle documentation to maintain compliance and operational readiness. Partner closely with manufacturing teams to resolve issues, improve system reliability, and minimize operational downtime. ​ Key responsibilities: System ownership, reliability, and operations Work with the capital project team to ensure systems are installed and operate safely, comply with pertinent environmental health and safety practices, rules, and regulations, and meet Amgen global engineering and design requirements. Serve as System Owner and Business Administrator for analytical equipment. Lead or work with teams in design, development and selection of new systems, instruments, calibration capabilities and consumable components. Development of laboratory equipment specifications to use for procurement of new laboratory equipment and instruments. Maintaining a current working knowledge regarding regulatory requirements for equipment qualification and calibration. Support in generation and resolution of protocol discrepancies as required . Alerting Quality Control Management if equipment fails to meet calibration or qualification requirements and conducting impact assessments/investigations as required . Lead the development of calibration/maintenance programs, ensure the availability of spare parts, schedule repairs and maintenance, and coordinate maintenance execution to keep systems in proper working order and minimize disruption to laboratory activities. Participation in technical project teams to function as a subject matter expert on instrument validation regulations and procedures. Evaluate the capabilities of current and potential suppliers, and assess new technologies that could provide cost savings, throughput, or other unique capabilities to Amgen manufacturing. Writing/contributing to equipment operating procedures and manuals. Designing and conducting training for manufacturing staff, and other department staff as applicable. Own and project manage change controls while meeting applicable change control metrics. Preparing and presenting periodic management updates on activities to senior management. Conduct periodic reviews of instrument validation as part of validation life cycle. Validation, compliance, and quality systems A key contributor to Data Integrity Assessments for Lab systems Support Amgen’s laboratory systems validation and Data Integrity philosophy during audit interactions. Support additional tasks and projects as assigned by management. Cross-functional support, projects, and continuous improvement Develop, coordinate, analyze, and present results for operational issues and engineering projects Provide technical support for commercial and clinical manufacturing as needed. Complete tasks under the general direction of lead engineers to complete design and engineering within schedule and budget constraints. Identify , support, and/or lead implementation of engineering-based improvements or upgrades in small to medium scope and complexity. Ensure necessary commissioning and qualification of systems is completed in alignment with site GMP requirements and support interactions with regulatory inspectors as necessary. Apply basic engineering principles and practices in support of daily operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of plant and process systems. Monitor systems to identify performance risks and implement risk reduction strategies. Provide troubleshooting support to reduce production downtime, including leading and/or supporting technical root cause analysis and implementation of corrective/preventive action; support may be required outside of normal working hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays. Support new product/technology introductions by performing engineering assessments, implementing equipment modifications, and supporting engineering runs. Advance the use of condition-based and predictive maintenance practices by incorporating advanced data analytics where applicable. Lead investigations of abnormal conditions through Deviation and related business processes. ​ What we expect of you We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The engineering professional we seek enjoys challenges and is motivated to help serve patients with these qualifications. Basic Qualifications: Master’s degree OR Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of cGMP laboratory, analytical instrument validation, and/or Process Engineer experience OR Associate’s degree and 6 years of cGMP laboratory, analytical instrument validation, and/or Process Engineer experience O R High school diploma / GED and 8 years of cGMP laboratory, analytical instrument validation, and/or Process Engineer experience ​ Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field Laboratory experience in a cGMP laboratory environment including exposure to analytical instrument validation. Knowledge of the methodology and instrumentation and analytical techniques used for biopharmaceutical testing. Understanding of current regulatory requirements for cGMP laboratory equipment validation and electronic record integrity. Demonstrated success in managing an equipment qualification or maintenance program. Ability to provide On-Call support coverage nights and weekends, on a rotating basis. Position requires strong written and verbal skills and the ability to work with minimum direction. Demonstrated interpersonal and facilitation skills and ability to work in a collaborative team-based environment. Ability to apply analytical skills to evaluate and interpret sophisticated problems using multiple sources of information. Ability to function within cross-functional teams and embrace a team-based environment. Work schedule flexibility as required to support 24/7 operations . Ability for domestic/international travel . What you can expect of us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way. In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers competitive and comprehensive Total Rewards Plans that are aligned with local industry standards. Apply now and make a lasting impact with the Amgen team! careers.amgen.com As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of diverse, ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease. Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by applicable law. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation. . Salary Range 88,281.00USD -119,439.00 USD

cold_email.subject: Interest in Rare Cardiac Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Rare Cardiac Coordinator opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Inventory Procurement Associate, Air
jobs.description: About the Team DoorDash Labs is an independent team within DoorDash. We explore robotics and automation to transform last mile logistics in the long term. If you want to work on commercializing autonomy and robotics in a service used by millions of people, then we want to talk to you! About the Role We’re looking for an Inventory Procurement Associate to support the sourcing, purchasing, and tracking of components critical to our robotics, autonomy, and field systems. This role is responsible for ensuring inventory accuracy, managing supplier relationships, and scaling procurement and supply chain workflows across hardware programs. You’ll work closely with engineering, sourcing, and operations teams to ensure timely and accurate delivery of components—from fast prototyping through production and early-stage deployment. This is a hands-on, operationally focused role within a fast-moving environment, with responsibilities spanning procurement, inventory management, and warehouse operations. The Inventory Procurement Associate will report to the Supply Chain team in our Autonomy Operations organization. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Source, negotiate, and purchase parts, tools, and materials for R&D, production, and field operations Build and maintain relationships with suppliers to ensure quality, competitive pricing, and on-time delivery Track and manage inventory across labs, warehouses, and deployment sites Receive, label, store, and issue materials used in R&D, production, and field builds Plan and kit materials for prototype, NPI, and production builds Submit and monitor purchase requests for a wide range of hardware components (mechanical, electrical, embedded systems, PCBAs, cables, packaging, consumables, etc.) Maintain organized records of POs, receipts, invoices, and part usage Conduct regular cycle counts and resolve inventory discrepancies Ensure proper storage practices for sensitive and high-value components Coordinate domestic and international shipments, ensuring compliance with customs, tariffs, and export regulations Support onboarding of new suppliers and ensure compliance with documentation requirements Help maintain procurement system workflows (Coupa, SAP, NetSuite, or similar) and resolve basic system-related issues Identify opportunities to streamline procurement, inventory, and warehouse processes Maintain and upkeep warehouse storage areas, implementing best practices in material handling, storage, and documentation Collaborate with cross-functional partners to forecast material needs and prevent shortages We’re excited about you because… You have 3–5 years of experience in procurement, inventory management, production, or hardware operations (preferably within robotics, aerospace, automotive, or manufacturing environments) You have experience with ERP and procurement systems (Coupa, SAP, NetSuite, or similar) and ideally MRP systems for production You are familiar with hardware development cycles, BOMs, and have supported engineering or R&D teams You have strong vendor management and negotiation skills You are highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong documentation and tracking skills You can manage multiple tasks, vendors, and requests in a fast-paced environment You’re comfortable handling everything from purchase order tracking to hands-on warehouse inventory management You’re proficient in Excel or Google Sheets for data analysis and reporting You’re able to lift up to 40 lbs and work in a hands-on lab/warehouse environment Bonus points… Experience supporting autonomy, robotics, UAVs, aerospace, or regulated hardware programs Familiarity with PLM systems (Arena, Agile) and BOM management Knowledge of international logistics, duties, tariffs, and shipping compliance Experience with low-volume, high-complexity parts procurement Proficiency in Jira and Confluence for workflow and documentation tracking Knowledge of lean inventory practices and supply chain optimization Forklift certification or demonstrated warehouse safety training Compensation jobs.title: Research Engineer, Infrastructure
jobs.description: WHY HARVEY At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. ROLE OVERVIEW As a Member of Technical Staff, Infrastructure in Harvey Research, you’ll build the systems that power how we adapt and improve leading open-weight models for legal work. We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. You’ll own the infrastructure behind that effort: distributed training, RL rollout systems, the environments where models learn to use tools and complete complex legal workflows, and the internal systems the team uses to manage data, run evals, and launch and track training jobs. You’ll help decide what we build, what we adopt, and how the pieces fit together. You’ll join a small, high-bar team of hands-on engineers and researchers, where each person owns a large part of the stack. We’re looking for research engineers who have built demanding ML or distributed systems, can debug across the stack, and want to work closely with researchers to make training faster, more reliable, and easier to iterate on. Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Scale our post-training stack, supporting SFT and RL on leading open-weight models. - Build distributed rollout infrastructure that coordinates model inference, tool execution, and collection of training experience for long-horizon tasks. - Build the infrastructure for reproducible agent environments where models can interact with documents, tools, and external systems during training and evaluation. - Own the performance and reliability of training runs, including GPU utilization, checkpointing, failure recovery, and observability. - Identify and remove bottlenecks across training and inference to shorten the path from research idea to useful result. - Build the internal tools and services the team runs on: training data management and versioning, running evals and browsing results, and launching and tracking training jobs and experiments. - Integrate models into production, including serving, latency, cost, and online evaluation, so research reaches customers quickly and safely. - Partner closely with researchers to turn experimental workflows into dependable systems while keeping room for rapid experimentation. WHAT YOU HAVE - Experience building ML infrastructure, distributed systems, or research tooling, with ownership of performance, reliability, and operation. - Strong Python and generalist software engineering skills across backend services, data systems, and internal tools, with familiarity with PyTorch, JAX, or similar ML frameworks. - Experience with distributed training or inference, including diagnosing performance bottlenecks and failures across the stack. - Understanding of post-training workflows; experience with RL rollouts, agent environments, or sandboxed tool execution is a plus. - Practical judgment about what to build versus adopt, and the ability to partner with researchers and ship quickly as needs evolve. We are hiring for this role across multiple levels. COMPENSATION $230,000 - $450,000 USD DEPENDING ON YOUR LOCATION, AN APPLICANT PRIVACY NOTICE MAY APPLY TO YOU. YOU CAN FIND ALL OF OUR APPLICANT PRIVACY NOTICES HERE https://harveyai.notion.site/Harvey-Candidate-Privacy-Notices-319ac3fcdd7a803bb807d5094f249922?pvs=74. #LI-DZ1 Harvey is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related condition, or any other basis protected by law. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities, and requests can be made by emailing accommodations@harvey.ai

jobs.description: Summary We are looking for an AI Engineer / Applied AI Scientist to help design, build, and deploy enterprise-scale Generative AI solutions that accelerate scientific, regulatory, and business processes. You will build intelligent applications powered by large language models (LLMs) , retrieval systems, knowledge graphs, agentic workflows, and advanced analytics. You will work closely with data scientists, statisticians, software engineers, domain experts, and business stakeholders to transform complex scientific and operational data into practical, production-ready AI solutions. As part of the R&D organization, the team also contributes to applied research, providing opportunities to contribute to scientific publications and conference presentations. Key Responsibilities Design, develop, and deploy Generative AI applications using modern LLM frameworks and technologies. Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines for enterprise knowledge retrieval. Develop agentic workflows for document processing, scientific applications, and research support. Integrate AI services and third-party APIs into enterprise platforms and production-ready applications. Build reliable, maintainable Python applications and services around AI capabilities. Experiment with AI-assisted software development tools, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub, and internal Pfizer tools, to accelerate application development. Evaluate emerging AI models, tools, and frameworks and assess their applicability to real-world use cases. Contribute to applied research projects, including scientific publications and conference submissions. Collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders to translate business and scientific needs into effective AI solutions. Required Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative or technical field. Relevant industry, academic, or research experience in software development, machine learning, data science, or AI (e.g., BSc with ~3 years of experience or MSc with ~1 year). Programming in Python. Working knowledge of core Generative AI concepts and architectures, including LLMs, RAG, and AI agents. Ability to independently develop and iterate on technical prototypes and turn ideas into working solutions. Strong communication and collaboration skills. Preferred Qualifications Experience with some of the following: REST API design and integration. React or other modern front-end frameworks. Vector & SQL databases. Git and GitHub development workflows. Linux environments. AWS or another major cloud platform. LLM evaluation, observability, or testing. Docker and containerized applications. Scientific, healthcare, pharmaceutical, or other regulated environments. Adaptability - Generative AI is evolving quickly. You're comfortable learning new concepts, tools, models, and frameworks and applying them pragmatically. jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary At BMS, digital innovation and Information Technology are central to our vision of transforming patients' lives through science. To accelerate our ability to serve patients around the world, we must unleash the power of technology. We are committed to being at the forefront of transforming the way medicine is made and delivered by harnessing the power of computer and data science, artificial intelligence, and other technologies to promote scientific discovery, faster decision making, and enhanced patient care. The Product Owner, Workday Adaptive Planning will co-own the product vision, roadmap, and backlog for BMS's Workforce Planning capability, built on Workday Adaptive Planning and integrated with Workday HCM — while also hands-on building and maintaining the Adaptive Planning integrations, security/permissions, reports, and dashboards that power it. Having established the foundational platform, this role will drive the next phase of the journey: maturing workforce planning from headcount and budget forecasting toward strategic workforce planning — including scenario-based org design, skills and talent supply/demand analysis, and long-range workforce modeling that directly informs business and talent strategy. This role partners closely with the business Product Manager, People Organization, and Finance leaders to translate evolving workforce planning needs into a prioritized backlog, and personally builds and maintains the integrations, security, reports, and dashboards that keep the platform accurate, secure, and trusted as the capability matures. If you want an exciting and rewarding career that is meaningful, consider joining our team! Key Responsibilities Workforce Planning Product Strategy Co-own, with the business Product Manager, the vision and multi-year roadmap for Strategic Workforce Planning, evolving the capability beyond current-state headcount/budget planning toward scenario planning, org design modeling, and skills/talent-based forecasting. Translate People Organization and Finance strategy into workforce planning requirements — e.g., how the business plans headcount, org structure changes, span of control, succession, and talent pipelines — and prioritize these in the Adaptive Planning backlog. Identify and prioritize opportunities to mature the model (new dimensions, planning versions, scenario types) as the business's workforce planning maturity increases. Hands-On Build: Integrations, Security, Reports & Dashboards Design, build, and maintain integrations between Workday HCM and Adaptive Planning, ensuring accurate, timely data flows for headcount, compensation, organizational dimensions, and planning versions. Configure and maintain Adaptive Planning security and permissions — roles, level and version access, and security groups — ensuring the right stakeholders can plan, model, and report at the right level of the organization, and that sensitive workforce data is properly protected. Build and maintain reports and dashboards (e.g., Adaptive Discovery Boards, OfficeConnect, Workday reporting) that give HR, Finance, and business leaders visibility into workforce plans, scenarios, and variances. Troubleshoot and resolve data quality, integration, security, and calculation issues directly, partnering with Workday HCM and Adaptive Planning admins as needed. Continuously enhance existing integrations, security configurations, reports, and dashboards based on stakeholder feedback and evolving workforce planning maturity. Adaptive Planning Model Design Own the backlog and hands-on build for Adaptive Planning models (sheets, dimensions, attributes, versions, assumptions) that represent the organization's workforce structure, positions, and headcount plans. Coordinate with stakeholders on cross-system interfaces (e.g., payroll, benefits, time & attendance) that feed or influence workforce planning assumptions, ensuring upstream/downstream data quality. Governance, Testing & Enablement Co-own governance and change control for the workforce planning product — model updates, assumptions, planning calendars, security changes, and integration schedules — aligning with enterprise SDLC and release processes. Own and execute testing and deployment (unit, system, UAT, regression) for integrations, security/permission changes, models, reports, and dashboards; ensure planning cycles (budget, forecast, headcount reviews) are supported without disruption. Drive stakeholder training and enablement for People Organization business partners, Finance, and leadership — model walkthroughs, scenario planning usage, and report/dashboard usage — to build organizational fluency as capabilities mature. Monitor adoption, performance, and data quality metrics to identify where the platform and process need to evolve next. Platform Currency & Innovation Stay current on Workday releases relevant to Adaptive Planning and HCM (planning features, security, integration enhancements, AI/ML-driven workforce insights) and assess fit against the strategic workforce planning roadmap. Champion best practices in workforce analytics and planning automation; partner with People Organization, Finance, and People Analytics teams to pilot innovations (e.g., skills taxonomy integration, predictive attrition/demand modeling) that move the capability toward strategic workforce planning. Provide leadership and guidance to cross-functional team members supporting the product, ensuring engagement and productivity. Qualifications & Experience Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Human Resources, Finance, or a related discipline. 5+ years of experience in HR or Finance technology, with strong exposure to workforce planning, Workday Adaptive Planning , and Workday HCM; product ownership or business analysis experience preferred. Hands-on, demonstrated expertise building and maintaining Workday Adaptive Planning integrations, models (sheets, dimensions, versions, assumptions), and security/permissions configuration (roles, level and version access, security groups). Hands-on experience building reports and dashboards using Adaptive Discovery Boards, OfficeConnect, and/or Workday reporting tools. Working knowledge of Workday HCM data structures (positions, organizations, worker/job data) and how they feed workforce planning. Understanding of workforce planning concepts — headcount and budget planning, org design/scenario modeling, position management, and (ideally) skills-based or talent supply/demand planning. Demonstrated experience owning or co-owning a product backlog, writing user stories/requirements, and prioritizing features in an Agile environment, ideally in partnership with a business-side Product Manager. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex integration, security, modeling, and reporting issues. Excellent communication skills, capable of translating technical concepts for People Organization/Finance stakeholders and business planning needs for technical teams. Strong stakeholder and project management proficiency, with proven ability to manage multiple initiatives concurrently and deliver within timelines. Knowledge of emerging Workday features ( Adaptive Planning , Prism Analytics, Extend) and ability to evaluate new functionality for roadmap fit. Leadership & Behavioral Competencies Strategic vision & maturity roadmapping: Sees beyond current-state capability to define what strategic workforce planning should look like and builds a realistic path to get there. Process & knowledge improvement: Leads analysis of current states; recommends pragmatic solutions and drives complex changes to completion. Foresight & change leadership: Stays current on emerging trends; identifies future state (org/tech/cultural) and builds transition plans aligned to enterprise vision. Systems thinking & judgment: Maintains broad perspective; applies analytical thought and creativity to structure work and select the best solution path. Collaborative partnership: Builds a strong working relationship with the business Product Manager, balancing shared accountability with clear communication on roles and decision rights. Preferred Skills (Nice to Have) Prior experience maturing a workforce planning function (e.g., from headcount/budget planning to scenario or skills-based planning). jobs.title: Product Growth
jobs.description: About the Team The Growth team drives user and revenue growth across ChatGPT’s consumer and business segments worldwide. We work across the full funnel, from acquisition and activation to retention and monetization, through product experiments, in-product improvements, performance marketing, creative development, and AI-powered workflows. The International Growth team works with regional leaders in priority markets to identify the user needs and product gaps that matter most for adoption, usage, and monetization. We turn country priorities into product roadmaps and growth plans, then partner with engineering, research, design, data science, marketing, finance, policy, and partnerships to test and ship improvements. We combine product strategy, product experimentation, with hands-on growth operations. We account for local behavior, competition, and product experience while building shared capabilities such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, and experimentation systems. We measure what ships, adapt it to the market, and scale approaches that work across markets. About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on Product Growth generalist with an international focus to help people get lasting value from ChatGPT across markets, use cases and product experiences. You’ll partner with international and central teams to understand user needs, identify growth opportunities and turn them into measurable improvements across acquisition, activation, engagement, retention and monetization. You’ll combine strong analytics and experimentation with product intuition, design judgment and a deep understanding of users and local markets. You’ll use AI-native automation and agentic tools to accelerate research, analysis, prototyping and execution. This role requires systems thinking and the ability to move across diverse experiences, improving both individual funnels and end-to-end workflows as products, user behavior and market needs evolve. You’ll be responsible for: - Partner closely with central SMB/Business teams to prioritize opportunities across markets, with clear hypotheses, owners, dependencies, and measurable outcomes. - Diagnose and optimize funnel performance using user research, event-level behavior, cohort analysis, and competitive insight. Identify drop-offs and high-value segments, distinguish local needs from shared product friction, and prioritize interventions. - Connect acquisition and marketing insights to product journeys; partner with regional marketers and channel specialists on tests that improve qualified acquisition and activation. - Own a rigorous experimentation program across onboarding, activation, repeat usage, re-engagement, paid conversion, and expansion. Partner with Engineering and Data Science on hypotheses, instrumentation, A/B tests and holdouts, readouts, and staged rollouts, with clear success metrics and guardrails. - Build and execute a focused international SMB growth roadmap, including in-product upsell, cross-sell, targeting, onboarding, activation/adoption, expansion, and monetization related experiences. Identify the use cases, onboarding barriers, product entry points, and upgrade moments that can improve adoption and sustained customer value. - Partner with Data Science and Engineering to develop, deploy, and improve classifiers and propensity models for segmentation, targeting, and personalized in-product journeys. Evaluate predictive quality and use controlled experiments to establish incremental activation, conversion, or expansion impact. - Own measurement across activation, retention, paid conversion, upsell, cross-sell, and revenue. Separate incremental impact from market mix, seasonality, or cannibalization, and use the results to decide what to scale, adapt, or stop. - Run a clear operating cadence with regional and central partners, surfacing international SMB results, trade-offs, dependencies, and decisions without requiring formal ownership of every team involved. - Build repeatable growth primitives, such as segmentation, lifecycle journeys, referral and expansion triggers, and experimentation tooling, that can be reused across segments and markets. Use AI-native workflows to accelerate research, prototyping, and iteration. We’re looking for someone with: - Experience across product growth, growth strategy and operations, data science, experimentation, and growth design systems, with hands-on ownership of product experiments and measurable outcomes in a fast-moving technology company. - A user-first track record of translating research and behavior into product priorities, then working with technical teams to ship improvements. - Deep expertise in funnel optimization and experimentation, including instrumentation, A/B testing, statistical power, holdouts, segmentation, cohort analysis, and interpreting incremental impact. A track record of turning experiment results into sustained product improvements. - The ability to work across product and marketing levers, connecting audience and acquisition insights to activation, retention, and monetization. - Analytical fluency in funnel modeling and growth economics, including incrementality, LTV, CAC, and payback; the ability to move between strategic prioritization and hands-on execution. - Practical experience applying classifiers and propensity models to growth problems with Data Science and Engineering, including choosing useful signals, evaluating model quality, and testing the impact of targeted interventions. - Ideally, experience scaling and continuously optimizing growth initiatives within Engineering and Data Science pods, from shared prioritization and implementation through experimentation and rollout. - Experience adapting products or growth programs across markets, with sound judgment about language, local behavior, business needs, and what should remain consistent globally. - Experience optimizing self-serve Business or SMB funnels and in-product upsell, cross-sell, or expansion journeys, or strong evidence of applying comparable growth expertise to a new customer segment. - The ability to influence central and regional teams, work independently through ambiguity, and carry an initiative from diagnosis through execution and evaluation. Workplace & Location - San Francisco or New York City based - Travel as needed for key cross-functional sprints and regional collaboration. Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Supervisor, Clinical Laboratory opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure — partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry. At the scale we build, our campuses are typically served by dedicated high-voltage substations and a medium-voltage distribution network that may also integrate on-site generation and battery energy storage — and the protection, control, and automation layer is what keeps all of it selective, coordinated, and observable. As a Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer, you'll own the protection and automation architecture across Anthropic's US portfolio — from the utility point of interconnection (POI) through the HV/MV substation, the MV distribution loop, and down into LV switchgear. You'll develop and maintain our protection philosophy and reference relay settings, run and review the short-circuit, coordination, and arc-flash studies that underpin them, design the substation automation and SCADA architecture, and define how relays and meters integrate into the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) — giving operators real-time visibility and sequence-of-events data when something trips. You'll also be our technical lead on the protection side of utility interconnection — working relay settings, transfer-trip, and ride-through requirements with transmission owners and ISOs/RTOs. Protection engineering and substation automation are the core of this role; substation physical design is a strong plus but not a prerequisite — we'd like to hear from protection and P&C engineers who have spent their careers on relays, schemes, and studies even if they haven't owned a substation general arrangement. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, our build partners' A/E firms, relay and switchgear vendors, and utility protection groups. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for witnessing factory acceptance and relay testing, and supporting site energization and commissioning. jobs.description: A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche. This role is in Early Development Biometrics (EDB), a core function within Product Development Data Sciences (PDD) that provides strategic leadership and scientific rigor across early clinical development at Roche. We partner across Biostatistics, Analytical Data Science, and Data Management to enable data-driven decision-making from first-in-human through proof-of-concept studies. As trusted partners in early development, we design efficient and innovative clinical trials, apply rigorous statistical methods, and implement high-quality programming and analytical solutions to accelerate timelines, de-risk development, and increase the probability of technical success. Our integrated teams operate with agility and scientific depth, supporting exploratory analyses, early regulatory engagements, and complex data-generation needs across therapeutic areas. Together, we bring scientific rigor, technical innovation, and strategic insight to shape the future of early development and deliver better outcomes for patients. Early Development Biometrics is also home to Methods Collaboration & Outreach (MCO), which enables the most impactful use of quantitative methodology across PDD through internal consultation, external collaboration, and continuous capability building; and Visual Analytics, which creates and maintains interactive dashboards that drive high-quality Medical Data Review (MDR) and safety signal detection, aligned with Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) principles and Critical-to-Quality (CtQ) endpoints. The Opportunity: The Real-time Visual Analytics Lead is responsible for driving the strategic direction, delivery excellence, and capability development of the Real-time Visual Analytics function within Early Development Biometrics. This role leads a team of Real-time Visual Analytics Specialists who create and manage interactive, study-level dashboards that enable high-quality Medical Data Review (MDR) and safety signal detection, aligned with Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) principles and Critical to Quality (CtQ) endpoints. As the Real-time Visual Analytics Lead, you will oversee the portfolio-wide implementation of visualization strategy, ensuring timely, scalable, and scientifically aligned delivery across early-phase studies. You will collaborate closely with biometrics leadership and clinical stakeholders to evolve visualization standards, guide implementation timelines, and optimize internal frameworks and tooling. You will also be responsible for talent development, process harmonization, and fostering a high-performing team culture focused on user-centered visual analytics, scientific rigor, and operational efficiency. Your leadership ensures that visualizations are not only technically robust but also embedded as a critical component of insight generation in early development. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Real-Time Visual Analytics (RVA) Lead opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Life Sciences (Large Molecules, Process Development)
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a research group focused on biological discoveries by combining AI with hands-on biological research. We're seeking a research scientist with deep expertise in antibody process development and manufacturing to join the team. Our goal is to speed up progress in the life sciences by an order of magnitude, and this role puts that mission into practice. You'll be an expert in making antibodies, with hands-on experience expressing, purifying, characterizing, and formulating them, from small screening batches to material for IND-enabling studies. Above all, you'll close the loop between AI-generated hypotheses and experimental data to share with the community. Working alongside AI researchers and engineers, you'll build and run the workflows that turn AI-designed sequences into well-characterized protein, and pressure-test AI predictions of expression, stability, and manufacturability against real data. This role is fully on-site in the San Francisco Bay Area. Key responsibilities Develop and run expression and purification processes for antibodies and other recombinant proteins end to end, including transient and stable expression in mammalian cells (HEK293, CHO), affinity capture (Protein A, IMAC), polishing chromatography, buffer exchange, and formulation Characterize what we make with the right analytical panel, for example SEC, CE-SDS, icIEF, LC-MS (intact mass, peptide mapping, glycans), DLS, thermal stability, endotoxin, and binding kinetics (SPR, BLI) Build the laboratory for this work, including selecting, installing, and qualifying equipment and setting up workflows that scale from plate-based production of hundreds of designs to gram quantities of a lead Evaluate AI-designed antibodies for manufacturability (titer, aggregation, stability under stress, viscosity, chemical liabilities), drive them to experimental readout, and feed results back to research teams Plan the chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC) path toward IND-enabling studies, from cell line development and scale-up to analytical methods and stability, and coordinate technology transfer and manufacturing with external contract manufacturers Ensure experimental data across programs is high quality and well documented, including batch records, methods, raw data, and failure modes Communicate findings clearly to biology, AI research, and life sciences audiences Minimum qualifications PhD in biochemical engineering, chemical engineering, biochemistry, or a related field Demonstrated experience in process development and manufacturing of antibodies or other recombinant proteins, including material supplied for IND-enabling or clinical studies, with recent, sustained hands-on laboratory work Comfort navigating ambiguity and defining problems in a rapidly evolving research environment Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively across cross-functional teams, with strong written and verbal communication skills Preferred qualifications 5+ years of biologics process development experience beyond the PhD Depth in both upstream (cell line development, bioreactors) and downstream (chromatography, filtration) development, with working knowledge of analytical and formulation development Experience setting up a protein production or process development laboratory, including laboratory automation and high-throughput, plate-based expression and purification Experience directing technology transfer and GMP manufacturing at contract development and manufacturing organizations, with contributions to the CMC sections of an IND Statistics or coding skills, for example design of experiments or Python for data analysis and automation Experience using AI or ML tools in the life sciences Publications and/or patents demonstrating scientific impact The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $300,000 — $320,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

jobs.title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle. The loads involved are large enough — and arrive fast enough — that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for. Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI). As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio. That means the on-site generation fleet — reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells — and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through. It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch. And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection. You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies — the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is. This is a deeply cross-functional role. You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against. You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs. Expect roughly 20–35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup. Responsibilities On-site generation engineering Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio — prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls — and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy — what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running Characterize the data center load for external generation partners — step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load — so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training — step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection — and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permanent power without stranding equipment or capacity Ensure generation designs meet NFPA 37, NFPA 110 where the plant provides emergency or legally required standby power, fuel-gas and fuel-storage codes (e.g., NFPA 54, NFPA 30), and applicable emissions requirements, and coordinate with environmental and permitting counterparts on the technical inputs to air permits Energy storage & microgrid architecture Size and specify battery energy storage systems for ride-through, step-load buffering, and power-quality support — including cell chemistry and enclosure selection, inverter selection (grid-forming vs. grid-following), UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A large-scale fire test data, and NFPA 855 installation requirements — and own the thermal and fire-protection interfaces Define the site microgrid topology and operating modes — grid-parallel, islanded, and black-start — and the transition logic between them, including load-shedding schemes, resynchronization criteria, and the conditions under which the site separates from and reconnects to the utility Specify the functional requirements for the microgrid controller — generation dispatch, set-point coordination across rotating and inverter-based sources, mode management — and drive its implementation, testing, and integration into site SCADA and the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) Help define the protection and control requirements for generation and storage sources so that interconnection protection, anti-islanding, and source-transfer schemes are consistent from the generator terminals through the point of interconnection Grid interconnection & power quality Lead the technical side of utility interconnection for sites with on-site generation or storage — interconnection applications, studies, and agreements, ISO/RTO processes, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and interconnection protection Own power quality at the point of interconnection — flicker per IEEE 1453, harmonics per IEEE 519, voltage regulation, reactive-power and power-factor requirements — and design the generation, storage, and filtering mitigations needed to keep the site within its interconnection limits under real training-load behavior Run or critically review the power-system studies that support interconnection and microgrid design — load flow, short-circuit contribution from rotating and inverter-based sources, transient stability, motor-starting and step-load studies, and electromagnetic-transient studies where inverter controls matter Vendor diligence & delivery Lead technical due diligence on on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, and microgrid-controller vendors — evaluating equipment and controls on engineering merit, stress-testing performance and availability guarantees, and reviewing proposed architectures against Anthropic's basis of design Define the technical performance terms in energy-services agreements with on-site generation providers — availability, power quality, ramp, and ride-through, each with a definition, meter, test protocol, and acceptance criteria — working with energy commercial and legal counterparts Review and disposition design packages, submittals, shop drawings, and deviation requests from generation providers and their EPCs, and hold partners to Anthropic's reliability and maintainability requirements Support commissioning of generation, storage, and microgrid systems — witnessing factory and site acceptance tests, defining and observing integrated systems tests (islanding, resynchronization, black-start, load-step), and resolving field issues against design intent Manage Trust and Safety success relies on our team being able to identify harmful situations, communicate empathetically with survivors, and make quick decisions to mitigate future risks. The goal is to provide the best support possible for those who have experienced an incident on the DoorDash platform and restore their status quo. This role appeals to you because you're a leader, operator, and owner. This is a tremendous opportunity to join a fast-growing team with an extreme focus on building DoorDash’s Trust and Safety brand while protecting our community. Operations Leadership and Culture Building: Operationalize strategic priorities while championing a connected team culture of learning, adaptability, operational excellence, and fun within the team. Liaison & Network Integrator: Represent PSM on Product Development workstreams as needed. Take the lead on maintaining a strong Portfolio network with peer groups in gRED, pRED, and GPS. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. Best,
Celina Lin

The Platforms Knowledge Management team's mission is to ensure Robinhood associates and customers have clear, current, and compliant guidance at their fingertips. We own the knowledge ecosystem — taxonomy, governance, editorial standards, and content lifecycle — and partner closely with CX Strategy, Product, Operations, Compliance, Legal, and Quality to publish SOPs and reusable messaging that are easy to find and use. As a Knowledge & Operational Readiness Specialist , you will own the content and readiness lifecycle for several assigned functions, partnering with senior team members on more complex work — driving knowledge strategy, leading readiness programs, and making meaningful program-level decisions with limited outside support. You lead cross-functional collaboration across all of your functions simultaneously, influence Product, Engineering, Compliance, and CX partners at all levels, and develop colleagues within the team. This is a role for someone who is equally fluent in SOPs and go/no-go frameworks, and uses AI to rethink what's possible.
